To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a longitudinal pattern recognition method based on principal components analysis improves predictive accuracy for disease classification and that this longitudinal information can also be used to transfer information across different groups of subjects.

(a) a longitudinal feature construction method can be used to improve the accuracy of disease classification in neuroimaging data and (b) the longitudinal information can be transferred from one dataset to another to improve the classification performance.

we developed a new longitudinal pattern recognition method, and applied it to two datasets to demonstrate that it can improve predictive performance relative to cross‐ sectional pattern recognition methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of longitudinal data for improving classification of subjects with neurodegenerative diseases.
developing and evaluating novel methods for improving the accuracy of disease classification using longitudinal neuroimaging data.
using longitudinal neuroimaging data in order to make predictions about disease status of individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach can be used to improve the classification accuracy of cross-sectional studies by using longitudinal data.
the use of longitudinal information can improve the accuracy of disease prediction, and that this improvement can be obtained without any a priori knowledge of disease‐related changes over time.
longitudinal data can be used to improve the accuracy of classification algorithms in a wide variety of settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel longitudinal pattern recognition method that can be applied to any type of longitudinal design and any number of time‐point measurements.
we propose a method for making use of longitudinal neuroimaging data for pattern recognition.

we developed a novel method that makes use of longitudinal information to improve predictive performance in pattern recognition tasks, which can be applied to neuroimaging data from a wide variety of longitudinal designs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can improve predictive accuracy of a classifier for a longitudinal dataset if we use longitudinal information in our feature construction method, as opposed to using cross‐sectional features.
longitudinal information can be used to improve predictive performance in pattern recognition tasks.
we show a way of using longitudinal information to improve predictive accuracy in pattern recognition.
